attempts.label: DANDI:001025
attempts.paper_title: Next generation CANCAN focusing for remote stimulation by nanosecond electric pulses
attempts.entry_title: NG-CANCAN focusing of electroporation and pulse voltage (Pakhomov et al. 2023)
attempts.summary: Only the voltage series of the paper's main findings could be tested here, and none of it reproduced. The 15- to 17-fold rise in dye uptake from 2.4 to 5.6 kV was not seen (ratios 5.7 to 7.3), possibly because the paper does not say whether background was subtracted. Focusing that does not depend on amplitude, in small and large arrays, also came out not reproduced, but this rests on an assumed ROI layout and, for the large array, two dishes against three. Single-cell bipolar cancellation could not be tested because those images are not on DANDI. The rotation, packet number, packet shape and electrode height findings appear to be in four sibling dandisets.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Pakhomov, Gudvangen, Mangalanathan, Kondratiev, Redondo and Semenov (2023) on dandiset 001025, which holds one stitched YO-PRO-1 image per dish for the experiments of Figure 7, Packet 2 rotated once on the small quadrupole array at 2.4 to 5.6 kV and ten times on the large array at 4.8 and 6.4 kV. The notebook finds the electrodes in each image, places the paper's ROIs along the diagonals and compares fluorescence and its normalised profile across voltages. The single-cell data of Figure 4 and the experiments of Figures 5, 6, 8 and 9 are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Pakhomov et al. (2023) from dandiset 001025

outcomes.statement: A single unipolar 600-ns pulse at 15 kV/cm causes by far the strongest YP uptake in individual CHO cells, 126 +/- 14 a.u. at the end of the 10-min recording (n = 25), and sham exposure causes no gain in YP fluorescence.
outcomes.quote: Sham-exposed cells showed no gain in YP fluorescence during the 10 min of observation. ... A single 600-ns pulse at 15 kV/cm caused by far the strongest YP uptake, reaching 126±14 a.u. (n=25) by the end of recording.
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds only monolayer images. The confocal time-lapse images of single cells between two electrodes (Section 2.2) are not in it, nor in any other dandiset that cites the paper (000686, 000875, 001027 and 001028 hold monolayer images of Figures 5, 6, 8 and 9); a search of DANDI for the lab's other dandisets found none that holds them.

outcomes.statement: Bipolar signals that start with the same pulse cause significantly weaker YP uptake than the single unipolar pulse (p < 0.001), reaching 20.8 +/- 2.0 a.u. for the 4-phase signal, 6.9 +/- 1.6 a.u. for the 8-phase signal and 25.4 +/- 2.8 a.u. for the 8-phase signal with 5-us delays; the 8-phase signal gives about 20-fold cancellation.
outcomes.quote: Bipolar signals started with exactly the same pulse (600 ns, 15 kV/cm) but caused significantly weaker effects (p<0.001). By the end of recording, YP signal reached only 20.8±2.0 a.u. for the 4-phasic signal; 6.9±1.6 a.u. for the 8-phasic signal; and 25.4±2.8 a.u. for the 8-phasic signal with 5-μs delays between phases. The impressive 20-fold bipolar cancellation achieved with the 8-phasic signal

statistics.about: each bipolar signal against the single unipolar pulse, end of recording

outcomes.notes: As fig4-unipolar-strongest; the single-cell time-lapse data are not public on DANDI.

outcomes.statement: Packet 2 applied 40 times from e1 enhances electroporation in the center of the array despite the weakening field, while the unipolar train control electroporates more strongly throughout and follows the field distribution; without rotation the region near e1 stays stronger than the center.
outcomes.quote: The lack of cancellation caused a much stronger electroporation throughout the array, and the distribution of YP uptake expectedly followed the electric field strength distribution in Fig. 3C . In contrast, Packet 2 enhanced electroporation in the center of the array, despite gradual weakening of the electric field with distance from e1. However, the bipolar cancellation only partially offset the electric field weakening, and electroporation near e1 remained stronger than in the center.
outcomes.notes: No dish of this dandiset received 40 packets or 40 trains from e1; its 21 images are the 1Px4 and 10Px4 treatments of Figure 7. The Figure 5 images appear to be in dandiset 000686 ("Focusing electroporation to the center of a quadrupole electrode array by interference of unipolar pulses"), which cites the same paper and is a target of its own; the claims file gives this claim as data from this dataset, so it is not tested here.

outcomes.statement: Rotating the first-energized electrode with Packet 2 (1Px40) smears the effect at the perimeter and emphasizes a remote effect in the center, while the same rotation of the unipolar train (1Tx40) leaves a void of electroporation in the center; the difference is clearest in fluorescence normalized to the most peripheral ROI.
outcomes.quote: Rotation with Packet 2 “smeared” the electroporation effect at the perimeter and emphasized the remote effect in the center. This remote effect contrasted with a void of electroporation in the center when the pulse train was applied in the same manner instead of the packet.
outcomes.notes: No 1Px40 or 1Tx40 dishes in this dandiset; see fig5a-center-enhanced-without-rotation (dandiset 000686).

outcomes.statement: Increasing the total number of rotated Packet 2 packets from 4 to 20 and 40 strongly increases YP uptake throughout the array, and the central peak is discernible for all three.
outcomes.quote: Increasing the total number of applied packets from 4 to 20 and 40 profoundly enhanced the electroporative YP dye uptake throughout the electrode array ( Fig. 6A ). The peak of electroporation in the center was clearly discernable for all tested treatments.
outcomes.notes: This dandiset has no 5Px4 dishes, and its 1Px4 and 10Px4 dishes are on different arrays (small and large, from the electrode spacing), so no packet-number series on one array. The Figure 6 images appear to be in dandiset 000875 ("Influence of unipolar pulse packet quantity on centering the electroporation effect"), which cites the same paper and is a target of its own.

outcomes.statement: Normalized to the periphery, the central peak is almost twofold for 1Px4 and about the same as the periphery for 5Px4 and 10Px4; the trough between center and electrodes is about twofold lower than the center for all treatments; the central peak becomes narrower with more packets.
outcomes.quote: Its brightness was almost twofold higher than at the periphery for a single packet was applied 4 times from different directions, or about the same as at the periphery for the rotation of 5 and 10 packets ( Fig. 6B ). Interestingly, the least affected area of the cell monolayer (between the center and the electrodes) showed about 2-fold lower fluorescence intensity than in the center for all the treatments. Also, the central peak appeared narrower (sharper) with increasing the number of packets.

outcomes.statement: On the small array with 1Px4, raising the first pulse amplitude from 2.4 to 5.6 kV increases YP fluorescence 15.5 times at the most peripheral point, 16.2 times half-way to the center and 16.8 times in the center.
outcomes.quote: when the first pulse amplitude was increased from 2.4 to 5.6 kV (and the amplitude of the other pulses in the packet was increased proportionally, see Fig. 2C ), YP fluorescence increased 15.5 times at the most peripheral point; 16.2 times half-way to the center; and 16.8 times in the center ( Fig. 7A ).
outcomes.notes: Without background subtraction, as the criterion fixes, the 5.6 over 2.4 kV ratios of dish means under the main reading are 5.99 at the most peripheral ROI, 5.65 half-way and 7.25 at the centre (4 dishes at 2.4 kV, 3 at 5.6 kV). Over all 18 readings they range from 5.11 to 6.35, 5.31 to 6.01 and 5.93 to 7.59, and none is within tolerance. Leaving out any one 2.4 kV dish changes them by at most 0.59, and dropping the end ROIs inside the paper's 5% exclusion zone gives 5.77, 5.84 and 7.25. With the median inside the needle footprints subtracted (150.7 a.u. on average at 2.4 kV, 375.9 at 5.6 kV), a variant the criterion excludes, the main reading gives 13.37, 15.87 and 15.16 (two of three within tolerance), 2 of 18 readings put all three within tolerance, and with the exclusion-zone ROIs also dropped all three are within it (14.88, 17.10 and 15.16). At the pixel size implied by the needle footprints (a variant) the ratios are 5.71, 5.45 and 7.32 without background and 14.17, 14.82 and 15.39 with it. The outcome turns on whether an offset was removed. The criterion says none is, "as in the Methods"; the Methods do not say, and whether the claims file reads the paper correctly here is asked of a reader in questions/001025.yaml.
deviations: The paper measured the ROIs in MetaMorph with the electrode positions known; the dandiset holds no ROIs or electrode positions, so the electrodes are found by fitting four dark disks to each image and the ROIs are placed from their centre (overlays in the notebook).

The pixel size is not in the dataset. 0.65 um is used, from the ORCA-Flash4.0 camera and 10x objective the files name, assuming no binning. The dark footprint of each needle has a median radius of 0.650 mm (large array) and 0.718 mm (small array) at this scale, against the 0.75 mm radius of the 1.5 mm needles (Section 2.3). The footprints rule out the round-1 variant at which the large diagonal is 8.4 mm (0.591 um), which puts the needle edge inside the paper's ROI span on both arrays and is dropped, but they do not confirm the camera scale; they imply 0.679 um (small array) and 0.750 um (large array), at which the large diagonal is 10.65 mm, further from the paper's 8.4 mm than the 9.23 mm of the camera scale. The camera scale is kept for the main reading and the footprint scale is run as a variant; it does not change this claim's result.

At the camera scale the paper's ROI spans (Section 2.4) end 0.12 mm (small array) and 0.22 mm (large array) from the needle edge, inside the paper's exclusion zone of 5% of the diagonal (0.25 and 0.46 mm). The spans are kept as the paper states them; a variant drops the end ROIs inside the zone.
ROI width across the diagonal is not given (Section 2.4); square ROIs are used, a choice that changes only how many pixels are averaged.
The packet is not named in the session descriptions ("CanCan protocol ... 12.5% lower"); Packet 2 is assumed, as in Fig. 7 and the dandiset's title.
The dandiset has 4 dishes at 2.4 kV where Figure 7 states n = 3; all four are used and each leave-one-out is shown.

outcomes.statement: Normalized to the most peripheral ROI, the profiles for different first pulse amplitudes fully overlap, so the spatial distribution of electroporation, and NG-CANCAN targeting, does not depend on amplitude within the studied range.
outcomes.quote: In contrast, changing nsEP amplitude affected the degree of electroporation but not its spatial distribution ( Fig. 7 ). ... When the YP emission was normalized to the most peripheral ROI, the data for different nsEP amplitudes fully overlapped ( Fig. 7B ).
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading 1 of 20 voltage pairs differs at p < 0.05, the normalised centre at 2.4 kV (108.6%) against 4.8 kV (136.9%), p = 0.0037; no half-way pair differs (smallest p = 0.12). The pair stays significant whichever 2.4 kV dish is left out (p = 0.0012 to 0.0116). The readings disagree, 10 of 36 (18 layouts by 2 normalisations) give no significant pair and 26 give one to five. With no effect, the chance of at least one p below 0.05 among the 20 uncorrected tests would be 0.64 if they were independent; they share groups and dishes, and a simulation of this design gives 0.47 with the two positions correlated as in the data (r = 0.64). p = 0.0037 would not pass a Bonferroni threshold for 20 tests (0.0025), which the criterion does not apply. The normalised centre means lie between 108.6% and 136.9% across the five voltages. With the footprint background subtracted (a variant the claims file excludes) the main reading finds no pair (smallest p = 0.18), and 30 of 36 readings find none; whether a background should be removed is asked of a reader (questions/001025.yaml). With the end ROIs inside the exclusion zone dropped, 4 of 20 pairs differ without background and 2 of 20 with it. At the pixel size implied by the needle footprints the same pair differs without background (p = 0.0279) and no pair with it (smallest p = 0.14). Over all ROIs of the folded profile, 23 of 220 tests are below 0.05.
deviations: Assumed the main reading of the ROI layout (92 ROIs over both diagonals, both diagonals averaged, one ROI centred on the array centre, raw ROI means, normalisation to the mean of the end ROIs). The paper leaves each of these open (Section 2.4; claims file, opening comment); the reasons are given in the notebook (the Fig. 5B legend averages both diagonals for rotated packets, the Methods give one ROI count, the paper reports measured values). The outcome rests on it, as 10 of 36 readings find no difference.
Electrode detection, pixel size, exclusion zone, ROI width and packet as for fig7a-amplitude-scales-uptake.
The voltages (2.4, 3.2, 4.0, 4.8 and 5.6 kV) are taken from the dataset, as the criterion says; 2.4 kV has 4 dishes where the paper states n = 3.

outcomes.statement: The independence of the normalized distribution from amplitude also holds when rotating multiple packets (10Px4) on the larger array.
outcomes.quote: The findings held true for rotating multiple packets and when using the larger array ( Fig. 7C and D ). Overall, our results show that NG-CANCAN targeting of electroporation does not depend on nsEP amplitude, at least within the studied amplitude range.
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds two voltages for the large array with 10Px4, 4.8 kV (2 dishes) and 6.4 kV (3 dishes). Under the main reading the normalised centre is 232.6% against 126.0%, p = 0.0494, and the half-way values do not differ (94.8% against 46.8%, p = 0.16). Both 4.8 kV dishes (270.6% and 194.7%) lie above all three 6.4 kV dishes (102.4% to 149.8%). 27 of 36 readings find no difference, and with the footprint background subtracted the main reading gives p = 0.0705 (25 of 36 readings find none), so the outcome rests on the main reading and a two-dish group; with 2 dishes against 3 a non-significant reading could not show the absence either. With the end ROIs inside the exclusion zone dropped the centre differs more clearly (p = 0.0173; 0.0089 with background subtracted). At the pixel size implied by the needle footprints the difference is gone (249.5% against 226.6%, p = 0.57; p = 0.25 with background subtracted), so the outcome also rests on the camera scale. The a.u. values rise from 4.8 to 6.4 kV at all three positions (ratios 3.53 at the periphery, 1.89 half-way, 2.00 at the centre).
deviations: Only two voltages, one with 2 dishes, where the paper shows Figure 7C and 7D with n = 3 and voltages marked in the figure; the others are not in the dandiset.

Assumed the main reading of the ROI layout, as for fig7b-targeting-independent-of-amplitude; the outcome rests on it, and on the camera pixel size (the footprint scale, a variant, finds no difference).
Electrode detection, pixel size, exclusion zone, ROI width and packet as for fig7a-amplitude-scales-uptake.

outcomes.statement: Remote targeting, within the studied limits, depends neither on pulse amplitude nor on array size, so findings from small arrays can be extrapolated to larger inter-electrode distances.
outcomes.quote: the remote targeting, at least within studied limits, did not depend on either the electric pulse amplitude or array size ( Fig. 7 ). We infer that findings from small electrode arrays can be extrapolated to larger inter-electrode distances.
outcomes.notes: The criterion requires fig7b-targeting-independent-of-amplitude and fig7cd-holds-for-large-array to be reproduced; neither is, under the main reading. The folded normalised profiles reach, at their first position (the mean of the two grid ROIs beside the centre, each dish normalised to its end ROIs), 109.5% to 140.1% on the small array (1Px4) and 145.0% to 212.3% on the large one (10Px4); the two arrays received different packet numbers, so array size is not isolated.
deviations: Rests on the main reading assumed for the two claims it depends on, on the camera pixel size (fig7cd), and on the claims file's reading that no background is subtracted.

outcomes.statement: Packets 1, 2 and 3 (4 kV, 1Px4) produce the same YP uptake in the center (215 to 235 a.u.), but Packets 1 and 3 cause much more uptake near the electrodes (250 to 350 a.u.) than Packet 2 (about 120 a.u.), p < 0.01.
outcomes.quote: All packets produced the same YP uptake in the center (215–235 a.u.), but Packets 1 and 3 caused drastically more YP uptake near the electrodes (250–350 a.u. vs ~120 a.u. for packet 1, p<0.01, Fig. 8A ).

statistics.about: Packets 1 and 3 against Packet 2, near the electrodes

outcomes.notes: All dishes of this dandiset received Packet 2; no Packet 1 or Packet 3 dishes. The Figure 8 images appear to be in dandiset 001027 ("CANCAN focusing of electroporation in a quadrupole array by different pulsing protocols"), which cites the same paper and is a target of its own. The 4.0 kV 1Px4 dishes here may be the Packet 2 group of Figure 8, but the comparison needs the other packets. Set against the paper's Packet 2 values (not deciding the claim), they read 614.9 a.u. at the periphery and 718.8 a.u. in the centre (353.8 and 457.7 with the footprint background subtracted), against about 120 and 215 to 235 a.u., and their normalised centre is 118.8% (137.3% with background subtracted) against 183%.

outcomes.statement: Normalized to the most peripheral ROI, YP emission in the center drops from 183% for Packet 2 to 83% for Packet 3 and 74% for Packet 1, so the packet with the strongest bipolar cancellation targets best.
outcomes.quote: The superiority of Packet 2 for CANCAN targeting is highlighted by the drop of normalized YP emission in the center from 183% for Packet 2 to 83% and 74% for Packets 3 and 1, respectively ( Fig. 8B ).

outcomes.statement: Raising the large array 1, 2 and 3 mm above the monolayer reduces YP emission near the electrodes 2.4, 6.4 and 9 times but in the center only 1.02, 1.4 and 3.8 times, raising the targeting efficiency (center over periphery) to as much as 600% at 2 mm.
outcomes.quote: Specifically, YP emission near the electrodes decreased 2.4, 6.4, and 9 times with 1-, 2- and 3-mm gaps (as compared to electrodes being in the same plane with cells); in the center, it decreased just 1.02, 1.4, and 3.8 times, respectively. Such disproportionally faster fading of the effect near electrodes boosted the CANCAN targeting efficiency (measured as a ratio of the effect in the center and at the periphery) to as much as 600% for the 2-mm gap ( Fig. 9B ).
outcomes.notes: No dish of this dandiset was treated with the array above the monolayer. The Figure 9 images appear to be in dandiset 001028 ("CANCAN focusing of electroporation in 3D"), which cites the same paper. The 6.4 kV 10Px4 large-array dishes here match the 0 mm condition, but the gaps are missing. Their profile is printed in the notebook. The centre ROI of the main reading is 126.0% of the end ROIs; the first position of the folded profile (the mean of the two grid ROIs beside the centre), the value used for discussion-independent-of-array-size, is 145.0%. The text gives no a.u. for the 0 mm group to compare them with.

outcomes.statement: With the electrodes above the monolayer, electroporation is restricted almost exclusively to the center of the array.
outcomes.quote: YP fluorescence images in Fig. 9C show that electroporation is restricted almost exclusively to the remote target (center) when electrodes are placed above the cell monolayer.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the 21 monolayer images of Figure 7. The images of Figures 5, 6, 8 and 9 appear, from their titles and descriptions, to be in four other dandisets that cite the same paper (000686, 000875, 001027 and 001028), which the dandiset does not mention, and the single-cell time-lapse data of Figure 4 are in no dandiset that cites the paper.

No pixel size is given (the ImageSeries resolution attribute is 96 or 1, not a pixel size), the array (small or large) is not stated, and the electrode positions, the electrode labels e1 to e4 and the paper's ROI measurements are not included. The array can be inferred from the electrode spacing, and it matches the protocol in every file.
7 of the 21 files name no detector, objective or channel, and the 5 large-array files hold a second channel labelled DAPI that the paper does not describe.

Subject ids do not identify dishes. sub-15 and sub-25 each hold two dishes imaged on different days under different protocols (2.4 kV 1Px4 and 4.8 kV 10Px4; 5.6 kV and 3.2 kV 1Px4), so the archive counts 19 subjects for 21 dishes, while each dish was used in one experiment (Section 2.1).

Figure 7 states n = 3 for every voltage. The dandiset has 4 dishes at 2.4 kV, 3 at 3.2, 4.0, 4.8 and 5.6 kV on the small array, and for the large array only 4.8 kV (2 dishes) and 6.4 kV (3 dishes). Which 2.4 kV dish the paper left out, and the other large-array voltages, are not documented.

Question for the paper's authors. Was a background (camera offset or the intensity of unlabelled regions) subtracted from the ROI values before the fold changes of Section 3.3 and the normalisations of Figure 7? The images have a dark floor of 33 to 81 a.u. that varies between dishes and sessions. Without subtraction the 5.6 over 2.4 kV ratios here are 5.7 to 7.3, against 15.5 to 16.8 in the paper; with the median of the electrode footprints subtracted they are 13.4 to 15.9.

Question for the paper's authors. How were the 92 and 224 ROIs laid out (per diagonal or over both, their width, which diagonals for Figure 7), what is the pixel size of the stitched images, and how is the 8.4 mm diagonal of the large array measured? At the 0.65 um pixel of the named camera and objective the electrode centres of the large array are 9.2 mm apart on the diagonal, and the paper's ROI spans end inside its own 5% exclusion zone; the needle footprints imply a larger pixel still (0.75 um, a 10.65 mm diagonal), at which the comparison of Figure 7D finds no difference. Under the readings of the layout, the voltage comparisons of Figure 7B and 7D find a significant pair in 26 of 36 and 9 of 36 readings, so the outcomes of fig7b and fig7cd rest on the reading assumed.
The session descriptions name the CANCAN protocol with 12.5% decrements but not the packet (Packets 1, 2 and 3 all use that decrement); Packet 2 is inferred from the dandiset's title and Figure 7.

The 4.0 kV 1Px4 dishes, the Packet 2 condition of Figure 8 if Figure 8 used the small array (its legend does not say), read 614.9 a.u. at the periphery and 718.8 a.u. in the centre, against about 120 and 215 to 235 a.u. in Section 3.4, so the paper's a.u. do not appear to be the raw image values, or these are not the Figure 8 dishes. The paper does not say how its a.u. relate to the images.
